title: Anxiety on the Lena Horne job and leaving at the Cocoanut Grove
summary: He read her snarling vocal style as aimed at him, grew so tense a doctor found high blood pressure, and gave notice in Los Angeles.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: What was it like, working with Lena?
Well, it was all right.
Was she temperamental?

Not with the trio. The only thing that got me with her, it was little things she would do, kind of snarl in her singing, and I thought she was snarling at me. But she wasn't, at all. It was just the way she put her song over. And that used to worry me. I was thinking, maybe I did something wrong, or something like that.
Oh, really? Yeah. Did anybody tell you --
No, I never did tell anybody about that, see.
Yeah.

But I told Lennie that I had to leave the group because I didn't think I was doing my job, see. And Lennie said, 'What's wrong with you? You've learned the numbers faster than any of the best readers we have. And you're playing the numbers fine. This was in Los Angeles, at the Cocoanut Grove, there. That's where I left them.'
So it affected you that much, that you --

Yeah, I even had pains running across here, and I went to the doctor. And one doctor told me I had heart trouble, I couldn't play tennis. And I didn't believe him. So that same day, I went to another doctor and he took my blood pressure and he said, "What are you so uptight about?" I said, "I'm not uptight about anything." He said, "It's got to be. Your wife leave you or something like that?" I said, "No, my wife is all right."
That's my other girl.

And I said, "So why you asking me that?" He said, "Your blood pressure shows you're uptight." I said, "Are you kidding?" And he said, "Who do you work for?" I said, "Lena Horne." So he said, "You can't be uptight with her." And when he said that, that just --
Registered.
Registered right in my head that that was what I was uptight about. And I went right back and put my notice in.
Isn't that something?
And, really, --
It wasn't anything.
No, it was nothing she had said to me at all. She had never said nothing to me.
No, yeah.
Anything like that. But it was just
the way that she was doing, -- Yeah.
-- and I figured I was --
It made you nervous.
Yeah, I figured it was me.
Yeah.
I'd been with her quite a little while, you see.
And the money was fairly good.
Oh, the money was good, very good. It was good.
